description: Faithful reproduction of OpenClaw's agent-side architecture for CUA. Six components (B1-B6) across three phases: Phase 1 builds independent modules (prompt builder, memory, session persistence), Phase 2 adds context management and tool wiring, Phase 3 integrates everything into the agent loop. IMPORTANT: Category C components (CUA SDK callbacks like ImageRetentionCallback, TrajectorySaverCallback, BudgetManagerCallback, PromptInstructionsCallback) are assumed directly reusable from the CUA SDK without modification. This assumption may be wrong — these callbacks may have undocumented constraints, incompatible hook signatures, ordering dependencies, or behavioral quirks when combined with our custom callbacks. Every story that uses a Category C component must verify it works as expected during integration, not just assume it. If a CUA callback doesn't behave as needed, file an issue and implement a workaround or replacement in agents/openclaw/ rather than patching the CUA SDK.

The fix is in convert_to_responses_api_format() in session.py: unnest content blocks into top-level Responses API items. This must apply to ALL models (not just OpenAI) since ALL agent loops dispatch on top-level type. Key insight: remove the _is_openai_model guard — ALL backends need this conversion.

userStories.description: As the agent harness, I want a subagent tool that spawns a secondary LLM call (text-only or with screenshot context) to handle reasoning subtasks (planning, analysis, summarization) without consuming main loop turns, so that the primary computer-use agent can delegate complex thinking to a cheaper/faster model while staying focused on VM interaction.

context.notes: Scope subject to change. Consider: should subagent see current screenshot? Should it have access to memory? What model should it use (--summary-model or dedicated --subagent-model)? How to prevent recursive delegation?

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: Unit tests pass — SubagentTool accepts a prompt string, calls litellm.acompletion, returns the response text
Level 1: SubagentTool respects model config (uses --subagent-model or falls back to --summary-model)
Level 1: SubagentTool has configurable timeout (default 60s) and token budget
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 50 — trajectory logs show agent invoked subagent tool at least once
Level 2: Subagent responses in trajectory contain task-relevant reasoning (not boilerplate)
userStories.notes: Scope subject to change based on what proves useful in practice. Start simple: text-only delegation with optional screenshot passthrough. Can evolve into full ComputerAgent delegation later if needed.

userStories.title: Tool: Visual Analysis (Figure/Image Reading)
userStories.description: As the agent harness, I want a visual analysis tool that sends a screenshot region (or full screenshot) to a VLM with a specific question, so that the agent can extract structured information from charts, diagrams, game UIs, and other visual elements without relying solely on the main model's implicit vision capability.

existingFiles: utils/evaluation.py (llm_vision_judge — existing VLM call pattern for reference)
context.reference: utils/evaluation.py (VLM call patterns with image encoding)

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: Unit tests pass — VisualAnalysisTool accepts a question + optional region coordinates, returns VLM response text
Level 1: Tool can operate on current screenshot (default) or a saved milestone image
Level 1: Tool uses configurable model (VLM provider via --visual-model or fallback)
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 50 — trajectory logs show agent invoked visual analysis at least once
Level 2: Visual analysis responses contain task-relevant observations (e.g., game state, UI element identification)
userStories.notes: Scope subject to change. Start with full-screenshot analysis with a text question. Region cropping and multi-image comparison can be added later.

userStories.title: Tool Audit: Identify Migratable OpenClaw Tools
userStories.description: As the project lead, I want a systematic review of OpenClaw's tool surface to identify which additional tools (beyond subagent and visual analysis) could be valuable for CUA computer-use tasks, so that we have a prioritized backlog of tool components to implement.

context.reference: openclaw/docs/concepts/ (explore all concept docs for tool-related patterns)
context.depends: None — standalone audit. Should inform future tool stories.

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Produce docs/tool-migration-audit.md listing all OpenClaw tools with: (a) what it does, (b) relevance to CUA computer-use, (c) migration complexity (low/medium/high), (d) priority recommendation
Level 1: Audit covers at least: file tools, shell tools, web browsing, memory tools, code analysis, messaging — classify each as migrate/skip/adapt
Level 1: For each "migrate" tool, identify the OpenClaw source file and the CUA integration point
userStories.notes: Pure investigation/documentation story. Output is an audit doc that feeds future PRD stories. No code changes.

userStories.title: Cross-Model Message Format Compatibility: Investigation + Test Suite
userStories.description: As the benchmark operator, I want to verify that the current message format (transcript replay, compaction summaries, memory flush) works correctly across model families (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Kimi K2.5) and in cross-model configurations (e.g., Anthropic for computer-use + OpenAI for summarization), and build a test suite to prevent format regressions, so that the harness is not silently locked to one provider.

existingFiles: submodules/cua/libs/python/agent/agent/loops/ (explore all loop implementations: anthropic.py, openai.py, etc.)
context.depends: US-OC-022 (replay format fix must be done first)
context.reference: submodules/cua/libs/python/agent/agent/loops/ (each loop's message format expectations)

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)

Level 1: Investigation report docs/cross-model-compatibility.md covering: (a) Anthropic loop format expectations, (b) OpenAI loop format expectations, (c) Gemini loop format expectations (if CUA supports it), (d) Kimi/Moonshot format expectations, (e) format mismatches found, (f) cross-model combinations tested
Level 1: Unit tests — replay messages round-trip correctly through each supported loop's format converter (mock the LLM call, test the message pipeline)
Level 1: Unit tests — compaction summary output from model A replays correctly into model B's loop (test all pairwise combinations: Anthropic↔OpenAI, Anthropic↔Gemini, etc.)
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 15 with openai/computer-use-preview — no API format errors from replay messages
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 15 with anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514 --summary-model openai/gpt-4o — compaction completes without format errors
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 15 with Gemini model (if computer-use supported) — document results even if it fails
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 15 with Kimi K2.5 (if computer-use supported) — document results even if it fails
userStories.notes: Models to cover: Anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-opus-4-6), OpenAI (computer-use-preview, gpt-4o), Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-pro or similar with computer-use if available), Kimi K2.5. For models without computer-use support, test only the summarization/flush path (as --summary-model). Cross-model test matrix: main-model × summary-model for all viable combinations. If a model family is not supported by CUA's loop system, document the gap and what would be needed.
